prompt_suffix: Render this as a clean educational diagram. IMPORTANT layout constraints: - Keep the entire diagram fully contained inside the canvas. - Center the diagram and scale it down if needed. - Leave at least 15% safe margin on the left, right, top, and bottom. - No text, arrow, line, box, icon, node, label, or table cell may touch or cross the image boundaries. - Prefer a balanced landscape composition for wide diagrams. - Use a clean white background and readable Open Sans, Clear Sans, Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, Segoe UI Emoji, SF Pro, sans-serif typography.

images.prompt: A diagram showing two probability distributions side-by-side. On the left, a bar chart representing a discrete Binomial distribution with parameters n=10 and p=0.3. The x-axis is labeled "Number of Successes (k)" with integer values from 0 to 10, and the y-axis is labeled "Probability P(X=k)". The bars show the probability mass at each integer k, with the tallest bar around k=3. On the right, a smooth, symmetrical, bell-shaped curve representing a continuous Normal distribution. The x-axis is labeled "Continuous Variable (x)" with a continuous range, and the y-axis is labeled "Probability Density f(x)". The curve is centered around its mean ($\mu$) and shows its spread based on its standard deviation ($\sigma$). The two plots are clearly separated to highlight the fundamental difference between discrete (countable outcomes) and continuous (measurable outcomes) probability distributions.

images.prompt: A diagram illustrating the concept of sampling. On the left, a large, diverse group of small, indistinct human figures represents the "Population." This group is enclosed by a large, dashed circle, signifying its vastness. On the right, a smaller group of distinct human figures, visually similar to those in the population, represents the "Sample." This smaller group is enclosed by a smaller, solid circle. A large arrow points from the Population to the Sample, labeled "Sampling Process," indicating the selection of a subset. Another arrow points from the Sample back towards the Population, labeled "Inference," emphasizing that insights from the sample are used to understand the larger group. The diagram visually reinforces that the sample is a manageable subset used to gain knowledge about the entire population.

images.prompt: A diagram showing a bell-shaped curve representing the sampling distribution of a statistic (e.g., sample mean). The peak of the curve is centered at the sample mean ($\bar{x}$). A horizontal line segment below the curve represents the 95% confidence interval, with its lower bound (LCL) and upper bound (UCL) clearly labeled. The area under the curve within this interval is shaded to represent 95% of the distribution, visually indicating the range of plausible values for the true population parameter. The small areas in the tails outside this central 95% region are lightly shaded or left unshaded, representing the remaining 5% (2.5% in each tail), which corresponds to the significance level ($\alpha$). Arrows point from the sample mean to the center of the interval, and from the LCL and UCL to their respective points on the x-axis, clarifying the interval's boundaries.
